output.summary: An annual flowering herb probably native to Macaronesia and the western and central Mediterranean, the opium poppy has grey-green foliage and large red, white or mauve flowers, often dark at the petal bases. Its rounded seed capsules release white latex when wounded, while its seeds and their oil are eaten and contain very low levels of opiates.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds are eaten whole, milled or roasted; their oil is edible. Seeds contain very low opiate levels, and the oil contains even less.
